title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jal, NM
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jal, NM
metaDescription: Jal sits right where Lea County's Northwest Shelf gives way to core Delaware Basin horizontal drilling. We buy mineral and royalty interests here directly, no listing.
heroLead: Jal sits close enough to the Texas line that the wells around it look a lot more like Winkler and Loving County drilling than the shallower production up near Lovington.
intro: This is one of the more active corners of Lea County for horizontal Bone Spring and Wolfcamp development, and it's where I'd point an owner who wants to understand why offers on Jal-area acreage tend to run stronger than shelf-side tracts further north.

sections.heading: Basin-edge geology near town
paragraphs: Jal sits close to the transition where Lea County moves off the Northwest Shelf and into the true Delaware Basin, which means multi-bench Wolfcamp and Bone Spring pay is generally thicker here than farther north around Lovington. Operators have run steady horizontal programs through this corner of the county for years.

sections.heading: Cross-border ownership patterns
paragraphs: Given how close Jal sits to the Texas line, we regularly see owners here who also hold interests in Winkler or Loving County just across the border. If that's your situation, tell us, since we can often value and close on interests in both states at the same time rather than running two separate processes.

sections.heading: Reading current permits before we quote
paragraphs: Because this corner of Lea County stays busy, we always pull the latest New Mexico Oil Conservation Division permit filings on sections around your tract before we make an offer. A permit filed in the last few months can meaningfully change our number, so we'd rather work off current data than an outdated estimate.

faqs.question: Why does acreage near Jal tend to price higher than acreage near Lovington?
faqs.answer: Jal sits closer to the core Delaware Basin, where Wolfcamp and Bone Spring pay is thicker and horizontal development has been more active than the shallower Northwest Shelf production farther north in the county.

faqs.question: I also own minerals just across the line in Texas. Can you handle both at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly work with owners who hold interests on both sides of the Texas-New Mexico line and can coordinate valuation and closing together.

faqs.question: What information do you need to start on a Jal interest?
faqs.answer: A recent division order or check stub is fastest. Without one, we can locate your interest through Lea County records and New Mexico Oil Conservation Division filings.

faqs.question: How current is the activity data you use for Jal-area offers?
faqs.answer: We check NMOCD permit and completion filings shortly before quoting, since this area sees enough ongoing drilling that stale data can undervalue or overvalue a tract.
